claude.result:
Weekly plans are in, and monthly costs are now rounded to the nearest cent. All 35 tests pass. I couldn't run the CLI by hand because my command to do so was blocked, so `subtrack add "Meal kit" 59.90 --every week` is covered only by the unit tests.

- **Adding weekly plans:** `--every week` works, and `weekly` is accepted as well, like `monthly` and `yearly`. The usage text and error message mention it.
- **Monthly cost:** a weekly plan costs its price × 52 ÷ 12 a month, so €12 a week shows as €52.00. `list`, `total`, `add` and `export` all use the same calculation. The CSV export used its own copy of the old truncating formula, which I replaced.
- **Rounding:** this applies to every cycle, so your €119.99 yearly plan now shows €10.00.
- **Renewals:** weekly plans charge every 7 days from `--since`, and `renewals` lists them like any other plan.

I also fixed two things you didn't ask for:
- **Saved weekly plans:** the code that reads the subscriptions file would have turned `weekly` into `monthly` when loading. Weekly plans now stay weekly.
- **Renewals order:** `renewals` sorted by the label text (so "10 Nov" came before "2 Nov"). I changed it to sort by the actual date, which matters more now that weekly plans add more rows.

I updated the README and changed the old test that expected truncation (`test/cycles.test.js`). I also added tests for the weekly cost and the weekly charge dates. I haven't committed anything.
